learn.b: こんにちは (konnichiwa) means hello. おはよう (ohayou) is good morning, and こんばんは (konbanwa) is good evening. Use them at different times of the day.
ありがとう (arigatou) means thank you. すみません (sumimasen) means excuse me or sorry. さようなら (sayounara) means goodbye.
Say はじめまして (hajimemashite) when you meet someone. Then say わたしは ○○ です (watashi wa ○○ desu), which means I am ○○.

qs.q: What does こんにちは (konnichiwa) mean?
qs.why: こんにちは (konnichiwa) is the standard daytime hello.

qs.q: How do you say 'thank you' in Japanese?
qs.why: ありがとう (arigatou) means thank you.

qs.q: Which greeting do you use in the morning?
qs.why: おはよう (ohayou) means good morning.

qs.q: How do you say 'I am Ken' politely?
o: ケン を たべます (Ken o tabemasu)
ケン が すき (Ken ga suki)
ケン に いきます (Ken ni ikimasu)
わたしは ケン です (watashi wa Ken desu)
qs.why: わたしは ○○ です (watashi wa ○○ desu) is the pattern for I am ○○.

qs.q: さようなら (sayounara) means goodbye.
qs.why: さようなら (sayounara) is used to say goodbye.

qs.q: Match each Japanese greeting to its meaning
Put these greetings in order from morning to night

learn.b: いち (ichi) is 1, に (ni) is 2, さん (san) is 3, よん (yon) is 4, and ご (go) is 5. In writing they look like 一, 二, 三.
ろく (roku) is 6, なな (nana) is 7, はち (hachi) is 8, きゅう (kyuu) is 9, and じゅう (juu) is 10.
おかあさん (okaasan) is mother and おとうさん (otousan) is father. いもうと (imouto) is younger sister. かぞく (kazoku) means family.

qs.q: What number is さん (san)?
qs.why: さん (san) is 3.

qs.q: How do you say 'five' in Japanese?
qs.why: ご (go) is 5.

qs.q: What does おかあさん (okaasan) mean?
qs.why: おかあさん (okaasan) means mother.

qs.q: How do you say 'father' politely?
qs.why: おとうさん (otousan) means father.

qs.q: はち (hachi) means seven.
qs.why: はち (hachi) means eight. Seven is なな (nana).

qs.q: Match each number word to its number
Put these numbers in order from smallest to largest

learn.b: ごはん (gohan) is rice or a meal. さかな (sakana) is fish and にく (niku) is meat. りんご (ringo) is apple and パン (pan) is bread.
みず (mizu) is water and おちゃ (ocha) is tea. たべます (tabemasu) means eat and のみます (nomimasu) means drink.
おいしい (oishii) means delicious. すき (suki) means like. ください (kudasai) means please give me.

qs.q: What does みず (mizu) mean?
qs.why: みず (mizu) means water.

qs.q: How do you say 'I drink tea'?
o: おちゃを たべます (ocha o tabemasu)
おちゃを のみます (ocha o nomimasu)
みずを たべます (mizu o tabemasu)
ごはんを のみます (gohan o nomimasu)
qs.why: のみます (nomimasu) is the verb for drinking, and おちゃ (ocha) is tea.

qs.q: What does おいしい (oishii) mean?
qs.why: おいしい (oishii) means delicious.

qs.q: Which food is りんご (ringo)?
qs.why: りんご (ringo) means apple.

qs.q: パン (pan) means bread.
qs.why: パン (pan) is bread, borrowed from Portuguese.

qs.q: Match each food word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I eat fish every day

learn.b: です (desu) is like am, is, or are. Add か (ka) at the end to make a question. がっこうですか (gakkou desu ka) means Is it school?
Polite verbs end in ます (masu). いきます (ikimasu) means go, きます (kimasu) means come, and みます (mimasu) means see or watch.
Change ます (masu) to ません (masen) for no. たべません (tabemasen) means do not eat. Use います (imasu) for living things and あります (arimasu) for objects.

qs.q: What does か (ka) at the end of a sentence do?
qs.why: か (ka) turns a sentence into a question.

qs.q: What does いきます (ikimasu) mean?
qs.why: いきます (ikimasu) means go.

qs.q: What is the negative of たべます (tabemasu)?
qs.why: Replace ます (masu) with ません (masen) to make a verb negative.

qs.q: Which sentence means 'There is a cat'?
o: ねこが あります (neko ga arimasu)
ねこを たべます (neko o tabemasu)
ねこが いきます (neko ga ikimasu)
ねこが います (neko ga imasu)
qs.why: Animals are living things, so they use います (imasu).

qs.q: がっこう (gakkou) means school.
qs.why: がっこう (gakkou) is the word for school.

qs.q: Match each verb to its meaning
Put the words in order: I go to school every day

learn.b: Change ます (masu) to ました (mashita) for the past. たべます (tabemasu) becomes たべました (tabemashita), which means ate.
Use ませんでした (masen deshita) for did not. いきませんでした (ikimasen deshita) means did not go. The past of です (desu) is でした (deshita).
きのう (kinou) means yesterday. けさ (kesa) means this morning. These words often come near the start of the sentence.

qs.q: What does たべました (tabemashita) mean?
qs.why: ました (mashita) shows past tense, so it means ate.

qs.q: What does きのう (kinou) mean?
qs.why: きのう (kinou) means yesterday.

qs.q: How do you say 'I did not go'?
o: いきませんでした (ikimasen deshita)
qs.why: ませんでした (masen deshita) is the polite past negative.

qs.q: What is the past of です (desu)?
qs.why: でした (deshita) is the past form of です (desu).

qs.q: ませんでした (masen deshita) is the polite past negative ending.
qs.why: It means did not, for example たべませんでした (tabemasen deshita) means did not eat.

qs.q: Match each present verb to its past form
Put the words in order: I watched a movie yesterday

learn.b: どこ (doko) means where. えきは どこですか (eki wa doko desu ka) means Where is the station? The word えき (eki) means station.
みぎ (migi) is right and ひだり (hidari) is left. まっすぐ (massugu) is straight. まがります (magarimasu) means turn.
びょういん (byouin) is hospital and ぎんこう (ginkou) is bank. ちかい (chikai) means near and とおい (tooi) means far.

qs.q: What does えきは どこですか (eki wa doko desu ka) mean?
qs.why: どこ (doko) means where, and えき (eki) means station.

qs.q: What does みぎ (migi) mean?
qs.why: みぎ (migi) means right.

qs.q: What does まっすぐ (massugu) mean?
qs.why: まっすぐ (massugu) means straight ahead.

qs.q: How do you say 'Please turn left'?
o: みぎに まがってください (migi ni magatte kudasai)
まっすぐ たべてください (massugu tabete kudasai)
ひだりに まがってください (hidari ni magatte kudasai)
ひだりは どこですか (hidari wa doko desu ka)
qs.why: ひだり (hidari) is left, and まがってください (magatte kudasai) means please turn.

qs.q: とおい (tooi) means near.
qs.why: とおい (tooi) means far. Near is ちかい (chikai).

qs.q: Match each place to its meaning
Put the words in order: Excuse me, where is the bank?

learn.b: でんしゃ (densha) is train and ひこうき (hikouki) is airplane. きっぷ (kippu) is ticket. りょこう (ryokou) means trip.
いくらですか (ikura desu ka) means How much is it? たかい (takai) means expensive or high. やすい (yasui) means cheap.
Use ○○が ほしいです (○○ ga hoshii desu) for I want ○○. きっぷが ほしいです (kippu ga hoshii desu) means I want a ticket.

qs.q: What does いくらですか (ikura desu ka) mean?
qs.why: いくら (ikura) means how much.

qs.q: What does でんしゃ (densha) mean?
qs.why: でんしゃ (densha) means train.

qs.q: What does たかい (takai) mean when talking about a price?
qs.why: たかい (takai) means high or expensive.

qs.q: How do you say 'I want a ticket'?
o: きっぷを みます (kippu o mimasu)
きっぷは どこですか (kippu wa doko desu ka)
きっぷが たかい (kippu ga takai)
きっぷが ほしいです (kippu ga hoshii desu)
qs.why: ほしいです (hoshii desu) means want.

qs.q: やすい (yasui) means expensive.
qs.why: やすい (yasui) means cheap.

qs.q: Match each travel word to its meaning
Put the words in order: How much is this ticket?

learn.b: おもしろい (omoshiroi) means interesting or fun. つまらない (tsumaranai) means boring. かんたん (kantan) means easy and むずかしい (muzukashii) means difficult.
Add と おもいます (to omoimasu) to say I think. おもしろいと おもいます (omoshiroi to omoimasu) means I think it is fun.
どうして (doushite) means why. から (kara) means because and goes after the reason. けど (kedo) means but.

qs.q: How do you say 'I think it is fun'?
o: おもしろいと おもいます (omoshiroi to omoimasu)
おもしろいを たべます (omoshiroi o tabemasu)
つまらないですか (tsumaranai desu ka)
おもしろいに いきます (omoshiroi ni ikimasu)
qs.why: と おもいます (to omoimasu) means I think.

qs.q: What does むずかしい (muzukashii) mean?
qs.why: むずかしい (muzukashii) means difficult.

qs.q: What does どうして (doushite) mean?
qs.why: どうして (doushite) means why.

qs.q: What does から (kara) mean after a reason?
qs.why: から (kara) after a clause means because.

qs.q: きらい (kirai) means like.
qs.why: きらい (kirai) means dislike. Like is すき (suki).

qs.q: Match each describing word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I think Japanese is interesting

learn.b: Latitude lines run east-west and measure distance north or south of the equator. Longitude lines run north-south and measure distance east or west of the prime meridian, which passes through Greenwich, England.
The equator splits Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres. There are seven continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America.
A legend explains the symbols on a map. A scale shows how map distance matches real distance. The Pacific is the largest ocean.

qs.q: Which lines measure distance north or south of the equator?
qs.why: Latitude measures north-south position.

qs.q: The prime meridian passes through which place?
qs.why: Greenwich is at 0 degrees longitude.

qs.q: How many continents are there?
qs.why: The common model counts seven continents.

qs.q: What does the equator divide Earth into?
qs.why: The equator is 0 degrees latitude.

qs.q: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth.
qs.why: It covers about one third of Earth's surface.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
pairs: Distance north or south of equator
Distance east or west of prime meridian

qs.q: Put these oceans from largest to smallest

learn.b: A peninsula is land surrounded by water on three sides. A plateau is high, flat land. A delta forms where a river meets the sea. An archipelago is a group of islands. Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level.
Weather is what the air is like today. Climate is the usual weather pattern over many years. Places near the equator are usually warm, and places near the poles are cold.
A biome is a large natural region, such as rainforest, desert, or tundra. Tundra has permanently frozen ground. Earth has four layers: crust, mantle, outer core, and inner core.

qs.q: Which is the highest mountain above sea level?
qs.why: Everest is about 8,849 meters high.

qs.q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
qs.why: The Sahara in Africa is the largest hot desert.

qs.q: What is climate?
o: The usual weather pattern over many years
qs.why: Climate is long-term; weather is short-term.

qs.q: Which biome has permanently frozen ground?
qs.why: Tundra has permafrost beneath the surface.

qs.q: Tropical rainforests receive very little rainfall.
qs.why: Rainforests are among the wettest places on Earth.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
pairs: Land with water on three sides
Land formed at a river's mouth

qs.q: Put Earth's layers in order from the surface to the center

learn.b: India and China have the largest populations in the world. Population density means how many people live in a certain area. Many people now live in cities, a trend called urbanization.

Migration is moving from one place to live in another. Push factors, like war or famine, drive people away. Pull factors, like jobs or safety, attract them. An emigrant leaves a country and an immigrant enters one.

Culture means the customs, beliefs, and language a group shares. Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers of any language. A capital city is the seat of government and is not always the largest city.

qs.q: Which two countries have the largest populations?
qs.why: India and China each have more than 1.4 billion people.

qs.q: What is urbanization?
o: Growth of cities as more people live there
qs.why: Urbanization means a rising share of people living in cities.

qs.q: Which is an example of a push factor in migration?
qs.why: Push factors drive people away from their home.

qs.q: Which language has the most native speakers?
qs.why: Mandarin has more native speakers than any other language.

qs.q: A country's capital city is always its largest city.
qs.why: For example, Canberra is Australia's capital, but Sydney is larger.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these settlements from smallest to largest

learn.b: Russia is the largest country by area, followed by Canada and China. The Nile flows through Egypt and the Amazon flows through Brazil.
Every country has a capital. Tokyo is the capital of Japan, Cairo of Egypt, Ottawa of Canada, Nairobi of Kenya, and Brasilia of Brazil.

Africa has the most countries of any continent. Australia is both a country and a continent. Oslo is far north, Rome is in the middle latitudes, Nairobi is near the equator, and Cape Town is in the far south.

qs.q: What is the capital of Brazil?
qs.why: Brasilia became the capital in 1960.

qs.q: Which continent has the most countries?
qs.why: Africa has 54 countries.

qs.q: Which river flows through Egypt?
qs.why: The Nile runs north through Egypt to the Mediterranean.

qs.q: Which country is the largest by area?
qs.why: Russia covers more than 17 million square kilometers.

qs.q: Australia is both a country and a continent.
qs.why: The country of Australia covers most of the Australian continent.

qs.q: Match each country to its capital
Put these cities in order from north to south

learn.b: Psychology is the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. Wilhelm Wundt opened the first psychology lab in 1879. Today psychologists study things like memory, emotions, and relationships.
Surveys ask many people questions. A case study looks deeply at one person. In an experiment, researchers assign people randomly to groups, so they can test cause and effect.
A correlation means two things are related. It does not prove that one causes the other. Only a well-designed experiment can show cause and effect.

qs.q: Psychology is the scientific study of what?
qs.why: That is the standard definition of psychology.

qs.q: Who opened the first psychology lab in 1879?
qs.why: Wundt's lab in Leipzig is seen as the start of modern psychology.

qs.q: Which method can show cause and effect?
qs.why: Experiments control variables and use random assignment.

qs.q: What does a correlation tell us?
o: Two things are related, but one may not cause the other
qs.why: Correlation does not prove causation.

qs.q: A correlation proves that one variable causes the other.
qs.why: A third factor may explain the link.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put the steps of the scientific method in order

learn.b: A neuron is a nerve cell. It receives signals through dendrites, passes them down the axon, and releases chemical messengers called neurotransmitters into the synapse, the small gap before the next neuron.
The cerebellum controls balance and coordination. The hippocampus helps form new memories. The amygdala handles fear and emotion. The frontal lobe helps with planning and decisions.
The brain has two hemispheres. The left hemisphere mostly controls the right side of the body, and the right hemisphere mostly controls the left side.

qs.q: Which brain part helps control balance and coordination?
qs.why: The cerebellum fine-tunes movement and balance.

qs.q: What is the main job of the hippocampus?
qs.why: Damage to the hippocampus makes it hard to form new memories.

qs.q: What are neurotransmitters?
qs.why: They cross the synapse to carry signals.

qs.q: Which brain part is most linked to fear and emotion?
qs.why: The amygdala processes fear and other strong emotions.

qs.q: The right side of the brain mostly controls the left side of the body.
qs.why: Each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put the path of a nerve signal in order

learn.b: Classical conditioning is learning by association, as in Pavlov's dogs, who learned that a bell meant food. Operant conditioning is learning from consequences. A reward after a behavior is positive reinforcement.
Memory has three jobs: encoding (getting information in), storage (keeping it), and retrieval (getting it out). Short-term memory holds about 7 items. Long-term memory is very large.
Spacing your study over several days helps you remember more than cramming. Testing yourself also strengthens memory.

qs.q: Pavlov's dogs showed which kind of learning?
qs.why: They learned to link a bell with food.

qs.q: A dog gets a treat after it sits. This is an example of what?
qs.why: Adding a reward makes the behavior more likely.

qs.q: About how many items can short-term memory hold?
qs.why: Miller's research suggested 7, plus or minus 2.

qs.q: Which study method best builds long-term memory?
qs.why: Spaced practice beats cramming for long-term recall.

qs.q: Long-term memory can only hold a small amount of information.
qs.why: Long-term memory has no known practical limit.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put the flow of information through memory in order

learn.b: Jean Piaget described four stages of thinking in children: sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete operational, and formal operational. Erik Erikson said people face a social challenge at every stage of life.
Abraham Maslow said people have a hierarchy of needs. Basic physiological needs like food and sleep come first, then safety, belonging, esteem, and finally self-actualization.
Conformity means changing your behavior to match a group. Obedience means following an authority. The bystander effect means people are less likely to help when others are present.

qs.q: Which psychologist proposed four stages of cognitive development?
qs.why: Piaget described how children's thinking changes with age.

qs.q: What is at the base of Maslow's hierarchy of needs?
qs.why: Basic needs like food and water come first.

qs.q: What does the bystander effect describe?
o: People help more in large groups
People are less likely to help when others are present
qs.why: Responsibility is spread across onlookers.

qs.q: What is conformity?
o: Changing behavior to match a group
qs.why: Asch's line experiments showed people conform to the group.

qs.q: Erikson proposed that people face a social challenge at each stage of life.
qs.why: His theory has eight psychosocial stages.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put Piaget's stages in order

learn.b: Water is polar, so its molecules form hydrogen bonds. This makes water cohesive and a good solvent. Proteins are built from amino acids, and nucleic acids are built from nucleotides.
Eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus; prokaryotes do not. Mitochondria make ATP, ribosomes build proteins, and lysosomes break down waste. The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves.

Osmosis is the passive movement of water across a membrane. Active transport uses ATP to move substances against their gradient. A secreted protein travels from the rough ER to the Golgi to a vesicle.

qs.q: What type of bond holds water molecules together, giving water cohesion?
qs.why: Polar water molecules attract each other through hydrogen bonds.

qs.q: What is the monomer of a protein?
qs.why: Proteins are chains of amino acids.

qs.q: Which organelle produces most of a cell's ATP?
qs.why: Mitochondria carry out most cellular respiration.

qs.q: What is the passive movement of water across a membrane called?
qs.why: Osmosis needs no ATP; water moves toward higher solute concentration.

qs.q: Prokaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
qs.why: Only eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.

qs.q: Match each organelle to its job
Put the path of a secreted protein in order
items: Made on a ribosome at the rough ER

learn.b: Enzymes are proteins that speed up reactions by lowering the activation energy. They are not used up. Temperature and pH can change an enzyme's shape and its activity.
Photosynthesis happens in chloroplasts. The light reactions in the thylakoid membranes make ATP and NADPH, and the Calvin cycle in the stroma uses them to build glucose from carbon dioxide.

Cells break down glucose in four steps: glycolysis in the cytoplasm, pyruvate oxidation, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain, which makes the most ATP. ATP is the cell's energy currency.

qs.q: What are the reactants of photosynthesis?
qs.why: Plants combine CO2 and H2O using light energy.

qs.q: Where do the light reactions occur in a chloroplast?
qs.why: Light-capturing pigments sit in the thylakoid membranes.

qs.q: Which stage of cellular respiration makes the most ATP?
qs.why: The electron transport chain drives ATP synthase.

qs.q: How do enzymes speed up reactions?
qs.why: Enzymes provide an easier path for the reaction.

qs.q: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and does not require oxygen.
qs.why: Glycolysis is the first, oxygen-independent step of respiration.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put the stages of cellular respiration in order

learn.b: Mitosis makes two genetically identical cells. Meiosis makes gametes with half the number of chromosomes, and crossing over and independent assortment create variety.
An allele is a version of a gene. Genotype is the genetic makeup and phenotype is the observable trait. A cross of Aa x Aa gives a 3:1 phenotype ratio when one allele is completely dominant.
In DNA, A pairs with T and C pairs with G. Transcription copies DNA into mRNA. In translation, a ribosome reads mRNA codons (three bases) and tRNA brings the matching amino acids.

qs.q: What does mitosis produce?
qs.why: Mitosis makes identical diploid daughter cells.

qs.q: Compared with its parent cell, how many chromosomes does a gamete have?
qs.why: Meiosis halves the chromosome number.

qs.q: What is the phenotype ratio of an Aa x Aa cross with complete dominance?
qs.why: Three offspring show the dominant trait for each one that shows the recessive.

qs.q: What does transcription produce?
qs.why: RNA polymerase copies a DNA gene into mRNA.

qs.q: In DNA, adenine pairs with cytosine.
qs.why: Adenine pairs with thymine; cytosine pairs with guanine.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put the steps of gene expression in order
items: tRNA brings amino acids matching codons

learn.b: Individuals vary, and some traits help them survive and reproduce more. Over generations, those traits become more common in the population. Mutations are the original source of new alleles.
Darwin and Wallace proposed natural selection. Speciation is the formation of new species, often after populations become isolated. A niche is an organism's role in its ecosystem.

Producers make their own food. Energy flows from producers to consumers, and only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level. A population is one species in an area; a community includes all species there.

qs.q: What does natural selection mean?
o: Individuals with helpful traits reproduce more
Traits gained in life are passed on
qs.why: Helpful heritable traits become more common.

qs.q: Who proposed the theory of natural selection?
qs.why: Charles Darwin published it in On the Origin of Species.

qs.q: Which group makes its own food in an ecosystem?
qs.why: Producers use light or chemicals to make food.

qs.q: About how much energy passes to the next trophic level?
qs.why: Most energy is lost as heat at each step.

qs.q: Mutations are the original source of new alleles.
qs.why: Mutations create new variation that selection can act on.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put this food chain in order, from producer to top consumer

learn.b: The atomic number is the number of protons. Isotopes have the same protons but different neutrons. Valence electrons are the outer electrons that take part in bonding.

Moving left to right across a period, ionization energy and electronegativity generally increase. Fluorine has the highest electronegativity. Electrons fill subshells in order: 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, and so on.
Ionic bonds form between a metal and a nonmetal when electrons transfer. Covalent bonds form between nonmetals when electrons are shared. A cation is a positive ion.

qs.q: What does the atomic number of an element tell you?
qs.why: Atomic number equals the number of protons.

qs.q: How does first ionization energy generally change across a period, left to right?
qs.why: Greater nuclear charge holds electrons more tightly.

qs.q: Which type of bond forms between a metal and a nonmetal?
qs.why: The metal gives electrons to the nonmetal, forming ions.

qs.q: Which element has the highest electronegativity?
qs.why: Fluorine attracts shared electrons most strongly.

qs.q: Electrons are found inside the nucleus of an atom.
qs.why: The nucleus has protons and neutrons; electrons are outside it.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these subshells in the order electrons fill them

learn.b: A mole is 6.022 x 10^23 particles, which is Avogadro's number. Molar mass is the mass of one mole in grams. For water, H2O, it is 18 g/mol.
Mass is conserved in a reaction, so both sides must have the same number of each atom. Balanced: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O.
The limiting reactant is used up first and limits how much product forms. Percent yield is actual yield divided by theoretical yield, times 100.

qs.q: What is Avogadro's number?
qs.why: One mole contains 6.022 x 10^23 particles.

qs.q: What is the molar mass of H2O in g/mol?
What is the limiting reactant?
o: The one in the largest amount
qs.why: It runs out first and stops the reaction.

qs.q: What are the coefficients that balance H2 + O2 -> H2O, in order?
qs.why: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O has 4 H and 2 O on each side.

qs.q: Mass is conserved in a chemical reaction.
qs.why: Atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put the steps of converting grams to particles in order
items: Start with grams of the substance
Divide by molar mass to get moles
The result is the number of particles

learn.b: An exothermic reaction releases heat and has a negative change in enthalpy (delta H). An endothermic reaction absorbs heat. Heat transfer is calculated with q = mc(delta T).

Rates depend on concentration, temperature, and catalysts. Higher temperature means more collisions with enough energy, so the rate usually goes up. Activation energy is the energy needed to start a reaction.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy and is not used up. Entropy measures disorder, and nature tends toward more disorder.

qs.q: What is true of an exothermic reaction?
o: It absorbs heat and delta H is positive
It releases heat and delta H is negative
qs.why: Exothermic reactions give off heat to the surroundings.

qs.q: What does a catalyst do?
qs.why: A catalyst gives a lower-energy path and is not consumed.

qs.q: How does raising the temperature usually affect reaction rate?
qs.why: More particles have enough energy to react.

qs.q: In q = mc(delta T), what does q stand for?
qs.why: q is the heat gained or lost, in joules.

qs.q: An endothermic process absorbs heat from its surroundings.
qs.why: Endothermic means energy flows in.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
pairs: Energy needed to start a reaction

qs.q: Put these temperatures in order from coldest to hottest

learn.b: At equilibrium, the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant. The equilibrium constant K is the ratio of products to reactants. Le Chatelier's principle says a system shifts to oppose a change.
An acid donates H+ and a base accepts H+. A strong acid like HCl fully ionizes in water, while a weak acid like acetic acid does not.
pH measures acidity. At 25 C, pH 7 is neutral, below 7 is acidic, and above 7 is basic. A buffer resists changes in pH.

qs.q: What is true at chemical equilibrium?
o: Forward and reverse rates are equal
qs.why: Both reactions continue at the same rate, so concentrations stay constant.

qs.q: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 25 C?
qs.why: Pure water has pH 7 at 25 C.

qs.q: If more reactant is added to a system at equilibrium, which way does it shift?
qs.why: Le Chatelier: the system uses up the added reactant.

qs.q: Which is a strong acid?
qs.why: HCl ionizes completely in water.

qs.q: A solution with pH 3 is more acidic than one with pH 5.
qs.why: Lower pH means higher H+ concentration.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these in order from most acidic to most basic

learn.b: A limit is the value a function approaches as x gets close to a number. For example, the limit as x goes to 3 of 2x + 1 is 7. The limit does not depend on the value at the point itself.
If plugging in gives 0/0, simplify first. For (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2), factor to get x + 2, so the limit as x goes to 2 is 4.
A function is continuous at a if the limit as x goes to a exists and equals f(a). A removable discontinuity is a hole. As x goes to infinity, 1/x goes to 0.

qs.q: What is the limit as x approaches 2 of (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2)?
qs.why: It simplifies to x + 2, which is 4 at x = 2.

qs.q: What is the limit as x approaches 3 of (2x + 1)?
What does continuity at x = a require?
o: The graph has a hole at a
The function is increasing at a
The limit exists and equals f(a)
qs.why: The limit and the function value must exist and match.

qs.q: What is the limit as x approaches infinity of 1/x?
qs.why: As x grows, 1/x gets closer to 0.

qs.q: If the limit of f(x) as x approaches a exists, then f(a) must be defined.
qs.why: A function can have a hole at a and still have a limit there.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these limits in order from smallest to largest value

learn.b: The derivative is the instantaneous rate of change, or the slope of the tangent line. The power rule says d/dx of x^n is n x^(n-1). The derivative of a constant is 0.
d/dx of sin x is cos x. d/dx of cos x is -sin x. d/dx of e^x is e^x. d/dx of ln x is 1/x.
The product rule says (fg)' = f'g + fg'. The chain rule handles composite functions: differentiate the outside, keep the inside, then multiply by the derivative of the inside.

qs.q: What is the derivative of x^3?
qs.why: Power rule: bring down 3 and subtract 1 from the exponent.

qs.q: What is the derivative of cos x?
qs.why: The derivative of cos x is -sin x.

qs.q: What is the derivative of e^x?
qs.why: e^x is its own derivative.

qs.q: Which is the product rule for (fg)'?
qs.why: Differentiate each factor in turn and add.

qs.q: The derivative of a constant function is 0.
qs.why: A constant has a flat graph with slope 0.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
pairs: d/dx of x^n is n x^(n-1)

qs.q: Put the steps for d/dx of (x^2 + 1)^3 in order
items: Identify outer u^3 and inner x^2 + 1

learn.b: If f'(x) > 0 the function is increasing; if f'(x) < 0 it is decreasing. If f''(x) > 0 the graph is concave up. An inflection point is where concavity changes.
Critical points occur where f' is zero or undefined. If f' changes from positive to negative at c, f has a local maximum at c. If it changes from negative to positive, it has a local minimum.
Velocity is the derivative of position, and acceleration is the derivative of velocity. Optimization uses derivatives to find the largest or smallest value.

qs.q: If f'(c) = 0 and f' changes from positive to negative at c, what does f have at c?
qs.why: The function rises, then falls, so c is a peak.

qs.q: If f'(x) > 0 on an interval, what is f doing there?
qs.why: A positive slope means the function is going up.

qs.q: What is velocity in terms of position?
qs.why: Velocity is the rate of change of position.

qs.q: Where does f(x) = -x^2 + 4x have its maximum?
qs.why: f'(x) = -2x + 4 = 0 gives x = 2.

qs.q: If f''(x) > 0 on an interval, the graph is concave up there.
qs.why: A positive second derivative means the slope is increasing.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put the steps of the first derivative test in order
items: Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x
Check the sign of f' on each side
Classify each point as max or min

learn.b: An antiderivative of f is a function whose derivative is f. The integral of x^n is x^(n+1)/(n+1) + C. For example, the integral of 2x dx is x^2 + C, and the integral of cos x dx is sin x + C.
A definite integral gives the net area under a curve between two limits. Riemann sums approximate it with rectangles.
The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus links derivatives and integrals: the integral from a to b of f(x) dx equals F(b) - F(a), where F is an antiderivative of f.

qs.q: What is the integral of 2x dx?
qs.why: The derivative of x^2 is 2x.

qs.q: What is the integral from 0 to 3 of 2x dx?
qs.why: x^2 evaluated from 0 to 3 is 9 - 0 = 9.

qs.q: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connects which two ideas?
qs.why: It shows integration and differentiation are inverse processes.

qs.q: What is the integral of cos x dx?
qs.why: The derivative of sin x is cos x.

qs.q: The integral of x^2 dx equals 2x + C.
qs.why: It equals x^3/3 + C.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put the steps for the integral from 0 to 2 of x dx in order

learn.b: In an experiment, the independent variable is what the researcher changes, and the dependent variable is the outcome measured. A placebo is an inactive treatment. In a double-blind study, neither participants nor researchers know who is in which group.

A correlation coefficient runs from -1 to +1. A value of -0.8 means a strong negative relationship. The median is less affected by outliers than the mean. Standard deviation shows how spread out scores are.
The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station. The hypothalamus controls hunger and body temperature. Neurons communicate with neurotransmitters.

qs.q: What is the independent variable in an experiment?
qs.why: Researchers change it to see its effect on the dependent variable.

qs.q: What does a correlation of -0.8 mean?
qs.why: It is close to -1, so as one variable rises the other falls.

qs.q: What is a double-blind study?
o: Only participants are unaware of groups
Only researchers are unaware of groups
Neither participants nor researchers know the groups
qs.why: This reduces bias from expectations.

qs.q: Which brain structure acts as a relay station for sensory information?
qs.why: Most sensory signals pass through the thalamus.

qs.q: The median is less affected by outliers than the mean.
qs.why: A single extreme score can pull the mean, but barely moves the median.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put the steps of an experiment in order

learn.b: In classical conditioning, a neutral stimulus gets paired with a natural one until it triggers a response alone. In operant conditioning, behavior changes because of consequences. Bandura showed observational learning with his Bobo doll study.
A variable-ratio schedule rewards behavior after an unpredictable number of responses, as with slot machines, and it produces high, steady responding.

Loftus showed the misinformation effect: misleading information can change memories. The availability heuristic judges how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind. An algorithm guarantees a solution if followed correctly.

qs.q: Bandura's Bobo doll study demonstrated which kind of learning?
qs.why: Children copied aggressive behavior they had watched.

qs.q: Which reinforcement schedule do slot machines use?
qs.why: Rewards come after an unpredictable number of plays.

qs.q: What did Elizabeth Loftus's research on memory show?
qs.why: This is the misinformation effect.

qs.q: Judging how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind is called what?
qs.why: Vivid or recent events seem more common.

qs.q: An algorithm guarantees a solution if it is followed correctly.
qs.why: Unlike a heuristic shortcut, an algorithm is a step-by-step procedure.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put the steps of classical conditioning in order
items: A neutral bell is paired with the food
The bell becomes a conditioned stimulus

learn.b: Vygotsky's zone of proximal development is the range of tasks a child can do with help but not yet alone. Erikson described eight stages, starting with trust vs. mistrust. Authoritative parenting mixes warmth with firm rules.

Freud said personality has an id (pleasure principle), an ego (reality), and a superego (conscience). The Big Five traits are openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism.
Intrinsic motivation comes from enjoying the activity itself. Extrinsic motivation comes from outside rewards or pressures.

qs.q: What is Vygotsky's zone of proximal development?
o: Tasks a child has already mastered
Tasks that are far too hard
Tasks a child can do with help
qs.why: It is the gap between what a child can do alone and with guidance.

qs.q: Which is NOT one of the Big Five personality traits?
qs.why: The Big Five are openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism.

qs.q: Which part of personality follows the pleasure principle in Freud's theory?
qs.why: The id seeks immediate satisfaction.

qs.q: What is intrinsic motivation?
o: Doing something for its own enjoyment
qs.why: The reward comes from the activity itself.

qs.q: Authoritative parenting combines warmth with firm rules.
qs.why: It is high in both support and expectations.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put Erikson's first four stages in order

learn.b: Major depressive disorder involves persistent sadness and loss of interest. A phobia is an intense, irrational fear. Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) helps people change unhelpful thoughts and behaviors. Schizophrenia and dissociative identity disorder are different conditions.
Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort felt when beliefs and actions do not match, which people often reduce by changing the belief. Prejudice is an unjustified negative attitude toward a group.
The fundamental attribution error means blaming another person's behavior on personality while ignoring the situation. Groupthink happens when the wish for harmony overrides good decisions.

qs.q: What does cognitive-behavioral therapy focus on?
qs.why: CBT targets the link between thoughts, feelings, and actions.

qs.q: Which is a main symptom of major depressive disorder?
o: Persistent sadness and loss of interest
qs.why: Sad mood or loss of interest lasting weeks is central to the diagnosis.

qs.q: What is cognitive dissonance?
o: Discomfort when beliefs and actions conflict
qs.why: People try to reduce the tension, often by changing a belief.

qs.q: What is the fundamental attribution error?
o: Blaming others' behavior on personality, not the situation
qs.why: We underestimate how much situations shape what others do.

qs.q: Schizophrenia is the same condition as dissociative identity disorder.
qs.why: Schizophrenia involves psychosis; dissociative identity disorder involves separate identities.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put the steps of systematic desensitization in order
items: Make a list of fears from mild to severe
Face the mildest fear while relaxed
Move up to the most feared item

qs.why: صباح (ṣabāḥ) means morning.

qs.why: Arabic script runs from right to left.

learn.b: मैं (maiṃ) is I and तुम (tum) is you. हूँ (hūṃ) is am and है (hai) is is. मैं छात्र हूँ (maiṃ chhātra hūṃ) means I am a student.
क्या (kyā) at the start makes a yes or no question. It also means what. कहाँ (kahāṃ) means where.
जाना (jānā) means to go and आना (ānā) means to come. स्कूल (skūl) means school. मेरे पास एक बिल्ली है (mere pās ek billī hai) means I have a cat.

qs.q: What does क्या (kyā) mean at the start of a sentence?
qs.why: क्या (kyā) starts a yes or no question and also means what.

qs.q: How do you say 'I am a student'?
qs.why: हूँ (hūṃ) goes with मैं (maiṃ) and means am.

qs.q: What does कहाँ (kahāṃ) mean?
qs.why: कहाँ (kahāṃ) means where.

qs.q: How do you say 'I have a cat'?
o: मैं एक बिल्ली हूँ (maiṃ ek billī hūṃ)
मेरे पास एक बिल्ली है (mere pās ek billī hai)
मैं बिल्ली जाता हूँ (maiṃ billī jātā hūṃ)
qs.why: मेरे पास (mere pās) is the way to say I have.

qs.q: है (hai) means 'is'.
qs.why: है (hai) is the present tense of to be for he, she, and it.

qs.q: Match each word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I go to school every day

learn.b: गया (gayā) means went and खाया (khāyā) means ate. मैं स्कूल गया (maiṃ skūl gayā) means I went to school. था (thā) means was.
Put नहीं (nahīṃ) before the past verb. मैं नहीं गया (maiṃ nahīṃ gayā) means I did not go.
आज (āj) means today and अभी (abhī) means now. पिछले हफ़्ते (pichhle hafte) means last week. कल (kal) means both yesterday and tomorrow, so the verb tells you which one.

qs.q: How do you say 'I ate food'?
o: मैं खाना नहीं हूँ (maiṃ khānā nahīṃ hūṃ)
मैं खाना पीता हूँ (maiṃ khānā pītā hūṃ)
qs.why: खाया (khāyā) is the past of eat.

qs.q: How do you say 'I went to school'?
qs.why: गया (gayā) means went.

qs.q: What does था (thā) mean?
qs.why: था (thā) is the past of to be.

qs.q: How do you say 'I did not go'?
qs.why: नहीं (nahīṃ) before the past verb makes it negative.

qs.q: कल (kal) can mean both 'yesterday' and 'tomorrow'.
qs.why: Hindi uses the same word कल (kal) for both, and the verb tense shows which.

learn.b: कहाँ (kahāṃ) means where. बैंक कहाँ है (baiṅk kahāṃ hai) means Where is the bank?
दाएँ (dāeṃ) is right and बाएँ (bāeṃ) is left. सीधे (sīdhe) means straight. मुड़िए (muṛiye) means please turn.
स्टेशन (sṭeshan) is station, अस्पताल (aspatāl) is hospital, and बैंक (baiṅk) is bank. पास (pās) means near and दूर (dūr) means far.

qs.q: What does बैंक कहाँ है (baiṅk kahāṃ hai) mean?
qs.why: कहाँ (kahāṃ) means where.

qs.q: What does दाएँ (dāeṃ) mean?
qs.why: दाएँ (dāeṃ) means right.

qs.q: What does सीधे (sīdhe) mean?
qs.why: सीधे (sīdhe) means straight.

qs.q: How do you say 'turn left'?
qs.why: बाएँ (bāeṃ) is left and मुड़िए (muṛiye) is turn.

qs.q: दूर (dūr) means far.
qs.why: दूर (dūr) means far away.

qs.q: Match each place to its meaning
Put the words in order: Excuse me, where is the hospital?

learn.b: कितने का है (kitne kā hai) means How much is it? महँगा (mahaṅgā) means expensive and सस्ता (sastā) means cheap.
टिकट (ṭikaṭ) is ticket, होटल (hoṭal) is hotel, and पासपोर्ट (pāsporṭ) is passport. ट्रेन (ṭren) is train and यात्रा (yātrā) means journey.
Say मुझे ... चाहिए (mujhe ... chāhiye) for I need or want. मुझे एक टिकट चाहिए (mujhe ek ṭikaṭ chāhiye) means I need a ticket.

qs.q: What does कितने का है (kitne kā hai) mean?
qs.why: कितने का (kitne kā) asks the price.

qs.q: What does महँगा (mahaṅgā) mean?
qs.why: महँगा (mahaṅgā) means expensive.

qs.q: What is पासपोर्ट (pāsporṭ)?
qs.why: पासपोर्ट (pāsporṭ) means passport.

qs.q: How do you say 'I need a ticket'?
o: मुझे एक टिकट चाहिए (mujhe ek ṭikaṭ chāhiye)
मैं एक टिकट खाता हूँ (maiṃ ek ṭikaṭ khātā hūṃ)
qs.why: मुझे ... चाहिए (mujhe ... chāhiye) means I need.

qs.q: सस्ता (sastā) means expensive.
qs.why: सस्ता (sastā) means cheap.

qs.q: Match each travel word to its meaning
Put the words in order: How much is this ticket?

learn.b: मज़ेदार (mazedār) means fun and उबाऊ (ubāū) means boring. आसान (āsān) means easy and मुश्किल (mushkil) means difficult.
मुझे लगता है (mujhe lagtā hai) means I think or I feel. मुझे हिंदी पसंद है (mujhe hindī pasand hai) means I like Hindi.
क्यों (kyoṃ) means why and क्योंकि (kyoṃki) means because. लेकिन (lekin) means but.

qs.q: What does क्यों (kyoṃ) mean?
qs.why: क्यों (kyoṃ) means why.

qs.q: What does क्योंकि (kyoṃki) mean?
qs.why: क्योंकि (kyoṃki) introduces a reason.

qs.q: What does आसान (āsān) mean?
qs.why: आसान (āsān) means easy.

qs.q: How do you say 'I like Hindi'?
o: मुझे हिंदी कहाँ है (mujhe hindī kahāṃ hai)
मुझे हिंदी पसंद है (mujhe hindī pasand hai)
qs.why: पसंद (pasand) means like.

qs.q: लेकिन (lekin) means 'but'.
qs.why: लेकिन (lekin) shows contrast.

qs.q: Match each describing word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I think Hindi is fun

learn.b: Say Hello or Hi when you meet someone. Say Good morning before noon and Good evening at night. Say Goodbye when you leave.
Say Please when you ask for something. Say Thank you when someone helps you. The answer is You're welcome. Say Sorry after a mistake.
Say My name is Ana. Then say Nice to meet you. To ask how someone is, say How are you? A common answer is I'm fine, thanks.

qs.q: Which greeting do you use in the morning?
qs.why: Good morning is the greeting for the morning.

qs.q: Someone says 'Thank you.' What do you answer?
qs.why: You're welcome is the polite answer to thank you.

qs.q: How do you tell someone your name?
qs.why: My name is ... is the standard way to give your name.

qs.q: Which word makes a request polite?
qs.why: Please makes a request polite.

qs.q: You say 'Goodbye' when you leave.
qs.why: Goodbye is used when you are leaving.

learn.b: The numbers are one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, and ten. We write them as 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10.
Your mother and father are your parents. Your brother is a boy in your family and your sister is a girl in your family. Family means the people who are related to you.
Say I have two brothers. For more than one, add s: one brother, two brothers. Use have with I, you, we, and they.

qs.q: Which number is 'seven'?
qs.why: Seven is the number 7.

qs.q: Your father's wife is usually your ...
qs.why: Your father's wife is usually your mother.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ two sisters.
qs.why: Use have with I.

qs.q: What is the plural of 'brother'?
qs.why: Add s to make most nouns plural.

qs.q: 'Sister' is a male family member.
qs.why: A sister is a female family member.

Put these numbers in order from smallest to largest

learn.b: Breakfast is the morning meal. Lunch is the meal in the middle of the day. Dinner is the evening meal. A snack is a small bite between meals.
Common foods are bread, rice, and apples. Common drinks are water and milk. We eat food and we drink drinks.
To order politely, say I'd like some tea, please. To say what you enjoy, say I like pizza. To say the opposite, say I don't like fish.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ water every day.
qs.why: We drink water. We eat food.

qs.q: Which sentence is a polite way to order?
qs.why: I'd like ..., please is a polite way to order.

qs.q: Which meal do you eat in the morning?
qs.why: Breakfast is the first meal of the day.

qs.q: Which of these is a fruit?
qs.why: An apple is a fruit.

qs.q: 'Delicious' means the food tastes very good.
qs.why: Delicious means very tasty.

Put the words in order to make a sentence

learn.b: Use am with I, is with he, she, and it, and are with you, we, and they. For example: I am a student. She is a teacher.
Use have with I, you, we, and they. Use has with he, she, and it. For daily actions, add s for he, she, and it: He goes to school.
Use don't with I, you, we, and they. Use doesn't with he, she, and it. For example: I don't like fish. She doesn't eat meat.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: She ___ a student.
qs.why: Use is with she.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: They ___ a dog.
qs.why: Use have with they.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: He ___ to school every day.
qs.why: Add es to go for he, she, and it.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ like fish.
qs.why: Use don't with I.

qs.q: 'He have a cat' is a correct sentence.
qs.why: It should be 'He has a cat.'

learn.b: For regular verbs, add ed to talk about the past. Play becomes played and walk becomes walked. We often use words like yesterday and last week.
Some common verbs change form. Go becomes went, eat becomes ate, see becomes saw, and have becomes had. You need to learn these.
Use didn't plus the base verb. I didn't go to school. Do not add ed after didn't.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: Yesterday I ___ pizza.
qs.why: Ate is the past simple of eat.

qs.q: What is the past simple of 'go'?
qs.why: Go is irregular, and its past simple is went.

qs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
qs.why: After didn't, use the base verb: come.

qs.q: What is the past simple of 'play'?
qs.why: Regular verbs add ed.

qs.q: 'I goed to the park' is correct English.
qs.why: The correct form is 'I went to the park.'

learn.b: Say Turn left or Turn right. Say Go straight to keep walking forward. Say Stop at the corner when you must stop.
Next to means beside. Opposite means on the other side. Between means in the middle of two things. Near means close and far means a long way away.
Start with Excuse me. Then ask Where is the bank? or How do I get to the station? These questions are polite and clear.

qs.q: Which word is the opposite of 'left'?
qs.why: Left and right are opposite directions.

qs.q: Which question asks for directions politely?
o: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
qs.why: It uses Excuse me and a full question.

qs.q: 'The bank is next to the post office' means the bank is ...
qs.why: Next to means beside.

qs.q: What does 'Go straight' mean?
qs.why: Go straight means keep going forward.

qs.q: 'Far' means a short distance away.
qs.why: Far means a long distance away. Near means a short distance.

qs.q: Match each phrase to its meaning
pairs: In the middle of two things

learn.b: A passport lets you travel to other countries. A ticket lets you take a train or plane. An airport is where planes land. A hotel is where you sleep on a trip.
Ask How much is this? to learn the price. Expensive means it costs a lot. Cheap means it costs little. A receipt is paper that shows what you paid.
Say I'd like to buy this, please. Say I'd like to book a room for two nights. You can also ask Can I pay by card?

qs.q: Which word means 'costs a lot of money'?
qs.why: Expensive means it costs a lot.

qs.q: You show this at the airport to travel to another country.
qs.why: A passport proves who you are when you travel abroad.

qs.q: How do you ask the price of something?
qs.why: How much is this? asks about the price.

qs.q: Where do you sleep when you travel?
qs.why: A hotel is a place to sleep on a trip.

qs.q: 'Cheap' means something costs a lot.
qs.why: Cheap means it costs very little.

Put the words in order to make a question

learn.b: Start with I think, I believe, or In my opinion. Say I agree if you think the same. Say I disagree if you think differently.
Because gives a reason. But shows a contrast. So shows a result. For example: I was tired, so I went to bed.
Use am, is, or are going to plus a verb for a plan: I am going to travel next year. Use more before long adjectives: more interesting. Use er for short ones: bigger.

qs.q: What does 'I agree' mean?
qs.why: To agree is to think the same as someone.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ going to travel next year.
qs.why: Use am with I in the going to future.

qs.q: Which word gives a reason?
qs.why: Because introduces a reason.

qs.q: What is the comparative of 'interesting'?
qs.why: Long adjectives use more in the comparative.

qs.q: 'Disagree' means you think the same.
qs.why: Disagree means you think differently.
